title: Plain-language tenant timeline and replay choices (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a customer-facing communications draft and internal runbook for account teams following the multi-region inference consistency incident on 2028-03-14. Goal: provide clear, non-technical timeline, summarize impact, explain verification steps customers can take, and present opt-in replay / remediation choices.

Summary for customers (one-sentence):
On 2028-03-14 between 02:04–06:20 UTC some requests processed across our EU and US regions experienced inconsistent outputs for a subset of model variants. We mitigated the issue by forcing a coordinated model pin and rolling cache flushes; no customer data was exposed.

What happened (plain language):
- Around 02:00 UTC a deployment change triggered a mismatch between two model-serving variants used by our routing layer.
- Some requests were routed to a model instance that was out-of-sync with the KV cache profile for prefix caching, producing inconsistent completions for certain prompts (not all requests).
- The behavior surfaced as customers seeing occasional truncated or context-shifted responses, primarily for longer conversations and streaming sessions.

How many customers were affected:
- Impacted tenants: approx. 120 tenants (0.8% of active tenants in the window).
- Request fraction: ~0.6% of total inference requests during the window.
- Data integrity: no persisted customer data loss; only output consistency anomalies observed.

Immediate actions we took (operator summary):
1) Identified routing imbalance and isolated the variant serving the mismatched KV cache.
2) Temporarily disabled automatic variant fallback and pinned traffic to the verified model variant in each region.
3) Performed coordinated KV cache flush + cold-warm restart of affected inference nodes to restore prefix consistency.
4) Deployed a hotfix to the routing policy to reject model variants without matching cache profile metadata.
5) Post-validation: ran synthetic prompt sets and customer-provided repro prompts to confirm restoration.

Short technical root cause (concise):
A deployment introduced divergent model-serving metadata (cache-profile id mismatch) between two compatible-looking model variants. Smart routing selected the variant without verifying the runtime cache profile, leading to stale prefix/KV usage and inconsistent outputs for in-flight sessions.

Customer actions you can take now (options):
- Option A (recommended for most customers): No action required. We restored services and validated behavior against canonical prompt sets. Continue normal operation.
- Option B (opt-in replay): If you observed incorrect outputs and want us to attempt automated replay of affected requests, reply to this message and opt in. We will: 1) isolate your affected request IDs 2) run replays against the pinned verified variant 3) provide evidence bundle and sanitized transcripts. Replays are offered for requests within the incident window only and require tenant consent.
- Option C (manual verification): Use the short checklist below to self-verify critical flows.

Quick verification checklist (tenant-facing, non-technical):
- Re-run 3 representative prompts that reproduced the issue. If they now match expected outputs, the issue is resolved for those flows.
- For streaming sessions, verify that token ordering and prefix continuity are preserved for sessions started before 02:00 UTC.
- If possible, provide one or two request IDs or timestamps to your Redwood contact to request more detailed evidence.

Replay/rollback constraints and notes: 
- Replays are best-effort and may not perfectly reconstruct external context (e.g., rapidly changing user prompt state).
- We will not modify your application state; replays are read-only.
- Replays can be rate-limited; we prioritize tenants with high business impact.
- If a tenant requests a rollback to a prior model variant, we can discuss options but rollbacks carry their own risk profile (latency/cost).

Customer-facing status snippet (for status page update):
- Summary: "Partial inconsistency observed for a small fraction of inference requests across EU/US regions. Edge cases affecting long conversational contexts verified and mitigated by 06:20 UTC. No customer data exposed."
- Impact line: "Intermittent inconsistent outputs for ~0.6% of requests (02:04–06:20 UTC)."
- Next steps line: "Offering opt-in replays for affected tenants; post-incident report and remediation plan to follow."

Postmortem summary for account teams (short):
- Root cause: deployment produced mismatched cache-profile metadata between model variants; routing lacked a final consistency gate.
- Contributing factors: gaps in pre-deploy variant metadata validation; insufficient synthetic prompt coverage for longer-session streaming scenarios.
- Immediate remediation completed: routing fix + cache flush + model pin.
- Planned longer-term fixes: metadata schema enforcement in CI, routing gating that checks cache-profile fingerprints, expanded synthetic tests for long-session streaming and prefix integrity, and additional dashboarding on cache-profile drift.

Draft customer email template (concise):
Subject: Update: Inference consistency incident (2028-03-14) — opt-in replays available
Hi <CustomerName>,
We conducted a service incident on 2028-03-14 that briefly caused inconsistent completions for a small subset of requests. We have mitigated the root cause and validated service restoration.
If you saw incorrect outputs and would like Redwood to attempt a read-only replay of affected requests, please reply to this message with "OPT-IN REPLAY" and include up to 3 example request IDs or approximate timestamps. We will follow up with results and evidence.
Thank you for your patience — we understand the importance of deterministic outputs, and we are prioritizing fixes to prevent recurrence.
Best,
Maya Thompson, Customer Success

FAQ (anticipate customer questions):
Q: Was any customer data read or leaked?
A: No. The incident only affected inference outputs; we have no evidence of data exfiltration.

Q: Will a replay change my historical logs or billing?
A: No. Replays are read-only and do not alter stored data. We will not bill for limited replay assistance performed as part of remediation.

Q: How long will replay take?
A: Most replays are completed within 48–72 hours. High-priority accounts can be expedited.

Appendix — evidence package and how to request it:
- Evidence we can provide on request: sanitized input transcripts, replay outputs (before/after), timestamped operator logs showing model pins and cache flush events, and validation run outputs.
- To request evidence or opt-in for replay: reply to your account lead or open a ticket referencing JIRA-INF-8342 and include tenant ID + up to 5 request IDs or time ranges.

Open questions / things to confirm before finalizing comms:
- Legal/Compliance review for wording around "no data exposure" (pending security sign-off).
- Confirm whether we should auto-offer replays to tenants with >500 affected requests (operational cost tradeoff).
- Finalize SLA credit language with finance if customers request replays and demonstrate business impact.

Notes to account teams (internal):
- Use plain-language snippet for customer outreach; attach the evidence bundle only after explicit customer opt-in.
- For enterprise customers, escalate to AE + solutions engineering for coordinated replay demos.
- Track all opt-in decisions in the incident JIRA (JIRA-INF-8342) and tag communications with CONF-1427.

This is a draft. Expect edits from SRE (Priya), Applied ML (Jonas), and Legal.
